required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh (n_rows, n_cols) output of x's dtype inside run().

Per row, the exact fp32 row max m and fp32 denominator l: either via the online rescaling recurrence over chunks (the running max is subtracted inside the recurrence) or directly over a row held on chip; held privately by the program that owns the row, never passed through global memory.
Per element, exp(x - m) / l with the final row statistics, in fp32, with one downcast at the store.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The whole operator is performed by a PyTorch softmax routine.
A tensor-method or library softmax replaces the online two-sweep kernel.
Host-side PyTorch reduction or exponential computes the row statistics outside the kernel.
Tensor-method statistics on the host replace the in-kernel reduction.
Atomics suggest a cross-program row reduction, which the contract forbids.
Exponentials appear to be evaluated in half precision; they must be fp32.
Writing into or returning the input violates the fresh-output / no-mutation rules.

required_evidence.message: No in-kernel max reduction found for the row maximum.
No in-kernel sum reduction found for the denominator.
No exponential primitive found in the kernel.
No fp32 upcast evidence; statistics and exponentials must be fp32.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (n_rows, n_cols) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with x

timing_boundary.notes: Measured: GPU time of all device work run() causes on every call (every kernel, fill, copy, cast). Host-side allocation, metadata reads and Python are not GPU time. No cached state across calls, no copy/cast/transpose of x, no global scratch for m or l, at most two logical traversals of each row.
